answer: Each agent must, for every action, recompute a proof tied to a physical knoll whose local topology forces a unique traversal path; because the traversal is bound to onyx veins laid down during the agent's first epoch, the cost grows as n² traversals rather than n parallelizable checks. A real limitation is that agents sharing the same ridge can shortcut the proof when they physically collaborate, collapsing the super-linear cost back toward linear if the hardware enclave is co-located.
